items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Willie had added George Johnson to the sax section and with me re-joining the orchestra, that made it eleven musicians and the only all-Negro American Orchestra in Europe. Wilson Meyers was on bass.

ctx.x: In a very short time Leon landed a job in a night club at Place Pigalle, but I didn't care much for the place and the band seemed to have lost something in it's style and gayety, so I gave my notice to Fess and rejoined Willie Lewis.

Willie had succeeded in getting Jack Butler in my place when I left for India but he was pleased to have me back in the band again. Willie had added George Johnson to the sax section and with me re-joining the orchestra, that made it eleven musicians and the only all-Negro American Orchestra in Europe. Wilson Meyers was on bass. I don't remember who Meyers came to Europe a second time with but he and I had been in Lucky Milliner's band together in Monte Carlo and Paris.

Willie's orchestra was working at the Ambassador which was a part of the Ambassador Theatre across the street from the American Embassy at Place de la Concorde. Shortly after I had rejoined Willie, Teddy Hill and his band came to Paris with a Cotton Club Revue and played quite a few weeks at the Moulin Rouge at Place Blanche. The revue was staged by Clarence Robinson who was very well known in Harlem for staging shows in the Cotton Club, Connie's Inn, the Lafayette Theatre, Harlem Opera House and the Apollo…
